title: §.XI Chemnitz: Cochlaeus at Worms 1540 and Pighius at Regensburg 1541 hated the fuller light — they would rather have kept the 1531 edition
pass_a_gloss: Indeed Cochlaeus at Worms in the Year 40 and Pighius in the Year 41 at Regensburg took it hard that by a fuller declaration on many Articles a great deal of light had come in. Whence they saw true opinions more illustrated and the shame of the Babylonian Thais more plainly stripped bare, and those men would rather have had the edition of the Year 31 simply retained, as their own writings testify.
pass_b_english: "Indeed Cochlaeus at Worms in 1540, and Pighius at Regensburg in 1541, took it hard that a fuller declaration on many articles let in so much light.
They saw true opinions set out more clearly, and the shame of Babylon's Thais stripped plainer still.
They would rather have kept the 1531 edition alone — their own writings say so."
source_text: Imò Cochlaeus Wormatiae Anno 40. & Pighius Anno 41. Ratisbonae graviter tulerunt, multis Articulis pleniori declaratione, plurimùm lucis accessisse. Unde videbant veras sententias magis illustrari & Thaidis Babylonicae turpitudinem manifestius denudari, & maluissent isti simpliciter retineri editionem Anni 31. sicut scripta ipsorum testantur.
